claims.statement: Morgen combines calendars, task systems, time blocking, booking links, and planning tools in apps for Windows, macOS, Linux, mobile, and the browser.
The Individual plan costs $30 monthly or $15 per month billed yearly. The Team plan costs $25 per seat monthly or $10 per seat monthly billed yearly, with at least two seats.
The trial lasts 14 days, requires no card, and the company states a 30-day money-back guarantee.
Combining several calendars and task lists in a flexible planning view is the strongest positive theme.
Cross-platform access, including Linux, and responsive support recur as positive themes.
Speed, mobile quality, accessibility controls, recurring task behavior, and price are meaningful limits in the sample.

scoreRationale.onboarding: Connecting accounts is only the start; a real week reveals whether the combined view removes checking or creates more of it.
scoreRationale.product: The unified plan is useful for people with several calendars and task systems, but sync, recurring tasks, mobile behavior, and speed are central reliability questions.
scoreRationale.support: Responsive help appears in the sample, but no urgent support case was tested.
scoreRationale.billing: The annual price is half the monthly Individual rate, which makes a complete trial important before a yearly commitment.
scoreRationale.overall: Morgen is worth testing when scattered calendars and tasks make daily planning hard. Keep it only if one messy week can be planned without checking every source behind it.

conflictsAndUnknowns: A combined view can save planning time only if changes return to the source systems correctly.
Desktop and Linux access are useful while mobile quality remains a reported concern.
Automatic planning may help with a busy week, but it does not excuse stale, duplicate, or misplaced work.
No hands-on sync, recurring-task, mobile, accessibility, scheduling, or support test was completed.
